# Running Activity Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

What the application is still working on, where to see it and get back to it, and what makes quitting ask first.

### Shape

#### Description

What counts as work still running in the application, and how each is listed, newest last.

#### Running

- the task the harness is working on, from the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor), headed "Task" with the first line of its prompt
- each question still running, from the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope)'s Ask tab, headed "Question" with its first line
- a spec build run on its own, as the [SpecBuildScope](../spec-build/index.md#spec-build-scope) says, "Building the spec"
- a divergence analysis in the [DivergenceScope](../divergence/index.md#divergence-scope), "Analyzing divergence"
- a search for concepts to rescope in the [RescopeScope](../rescope/index.md#rescope-scope), "Finding scopes to extract"
- a run target of the [RunTargetsScope](../run-targets/index.md#run-targets-scope) running, "Running" then its name, or its targets being found, "Finding how to run"

Prompts waiting in the queue don't count as running, since they are saved with the project, and neither does a panel whose work is over.
Everything running counts in every open project of the [OpenProjectsScope](../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope), not only the one on screen. Those of the project on screen come first, then each other project's, its rows headed with that project's folder name after the kind, such as "Task · my-project".

#### Indicator

While anything is running, a small spinner shows, with how many things are running beside it when more than one is. Its tooltip says what is running, or how many things are. While nothing is, neither shows, and nothing takes their place. Where it sits is up to what holds it.

#### List

Clicking the spinner opens a small list beneath it of everything running, one row each, in the order above, each with a small spinner of its own. Clicking a row closes the list and reveals what it is, first switching to its project when it belongs to another:

- a task brings back the latest task's output, closing the previous tasks and any inset panel over it, and scrolls it to the end
- a question closes the answer drawer and any inset panel, so its row is in view
- a divergence analysis, a rescope search, or a run target brings its [MinimizablePanelScope](../../ui/components/minimizable-panel/index.md#minimizable-panel-scope) back
- a spec build has nothing to show, so its row only closes the list

Pressing the mouse outside the list, or <Escape>, closes it too, as does everything in it finishing.

#### Quitting

Quitting, however it is asked for, while the harness is working on a task or a question, or while a spec build runs on its own, in any open project, asks first. A divergence analysis, a rescope search, or a run target doesn't ask, and quitting stops it. The message is titled "Quit while a task is running?" and says what is still running: the harness working on a prompt, piton build, or both, and, when it runs in more than one project, in how many projects. "Quit" exits, and "Keep Running" or <Escape> dismisses it. Asking to quit again while it is open doesn't open a second one, and an open palette closes first.

use /lib
use /ui
from ./application-tab import RibbonApplicationTabScope
from ./code-tab import RibbonCodeTabScope
from ./project-tab import RibbonProjectTabScope
from ./research-tab import RibbonResearchTabScope
from ./spec-tab import RibbonSpecTabScope
from /scope/running-activity import RunningActivityScope
from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope
from /ui/components/project-indicator import ProjectIndicator
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope

export ui-component RibbonScope:
    concept: {RibbonConcept}

concept RibbonConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the
        application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

    shape: {RibbonShape}

shape RibbonShape:
    description:
        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, in the colours of the
        @{ThemeScope}, a row of tabs, 32 pixels tall, above the command area. The
        tabs are flat: each is only its label, with 8 pixels either side of
        it, and no borders, no rounded corners, and no line anywhere, neither
        between the tabs nor between the tab row and the commands. The tab row
        has a background of its own, a step lighter than the command area,
        #333333 in dark mode; a closed tab has no background, and an open tab
        takes the command area's background, #222222 in dark mode, so it and
        the commands beneath it read as one piece, the edge of the colour the
        only edge. In light mode the same steps run the other way, the tab row
        a step darker than the command area. Opening and closing tabs never
        shifts a label.

        A tab whose commands work on one of the chat input's modes, as the Code
        and Spec tabs do, takes that mode's colour: its label is in the mode's
        colour while the tab is closed, and while open, the tab is tinted with
        it instead and its label is the tab's own colour. Each such tab says
        more. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on
        Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups.
        There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

    keyboard:
        <Alt+1> opens the first tab, <Alt+2> the second, and so on, through
        each tab in the order the tabs are shown, <Alt+5> opening Application.
        Each opens its tab alone, as clicking it does, and expands the ribbon
        first if it is collapsed. A number past the last tab does nothing. Like
        the ribbon's other shortcuts, they do nothing while an inset panel is
        open. A tab's tooltip doesn't give its shortcut, since a tab has no
        tooltip.

    openingSeveralTabs:
        Clicking a tab opens it alone, as usual. Ctrl+clicking one (Cmd+click on
        macOS) opens it alongside whichever tabs are already open, or, if it is
        already open, closes it, so any number of tabs can be open at once. The
        last open tab can't be closed this way: Ctrl+clicking it leaves it open.
        Every open tab shows as selected.

        The command area then holds the groups of every open tab side by side,
        in the order of the tabs rather than the order they were opened, with the
        same divider between one tab's groups and the next as between any
        groups. An
        open tab with no commands adds nothing, and "No commands yet" shows only
        when none of the open tabs has any. When the groups are wider than the
        window, the command area scrolls sideways. The command area stays the
        same height however many tabs are open.

        Double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon, and expanding it again
        shows the same tabs open. Which tabs are open isn't kept between
        launches: the window always opens with only Project open.

    leftContainer:
        At the left end of the bar, left of the tab bar itself rather than
        inside it, so the tab bar's own padding and bottom line don't reach
        it, sits the left container. It holds, in order, the project
        indicator, the collapse chevron, and the activity spinner, and can
        hold other things after them. It is the same whether the ribbon is
        expanded, beside the tabs, or collapsed, leading the row of primary
        commands.

        It runs from the top of the bar down to the line along its bottom,
        never over it, so it is the same height expanded and collapsed.
        Everything in it is vertically centred in that height, with no gap
        between one thing and the next and no padding around them: each
        thing's own size is all the room it takes. The container shrinks to
        fit what it holds, and when it holds nothing, it isn't there at all.

    rightContainer:
        At the right end of the bar, right of the tabs, or of the primary
        commands when the ribbon is collapsed, sits the right container. It
        holds nothing yet, and can hold other things. It lays out what it
        holds as the left container does: vertically centred, with no gap
        between things and no padding around them, shrinking to fit, and not
        there at all while it holds nothing, as it is now.

    activity:
        The indicator and list of the @{RunningActivityScope} sit in the left
        container, just right of the collapse chevron. While nothing is
        running, the spinner isn't there, and the left container shrinks
        around the project indicator and the chevron.

    projectIndicator:
        The @{ProjectIndicator} leads the left container, a solid block the
        full height of the bar down to the line along its bottom, ending on
        that line. It is the same height, and what it shows is in the same
        place, whether the ribbon is expanded or collapsed. There is no divider
        between it and what
        follows: the change of background is the edge. The collapse chevron
        sits just after it, and the activity spinner just after the
        chevron.

    groups:
        Groups have no titles shown. They sit side by side, and between one
        group and the next, 4 pixels from the buttons either side, stands a
        divider: a bar 4 pixels wide, in the tab row's background colour, as
        tall as the buttons, from the top of the first to the bottom of the
        last, with its ends softly rounded. The first group starts 8 pixels
        from the command area's left edge. Each group still has a name, saying
        what its commands have in common, which is the divider's tooltip and
        what assistive technology reads for it.

        A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

    tabs:
        Each tab is a scope of its own, which says what groups and commands it
        holds, and what each command does.

        project: @{RibbonProjectTabScope}

        code: @{RibbonCodeTabScope}

        spec: @{RibbonSpecTabScope}

        research: @{RibbonResearchTabScope}

        application: @{RibbonApplicationTabScope}

content.text:
The activity spinner now sits at the far right of the ribbon's tab bar, and the collapse/expand chevron button is gone. The ribbon still collapses by double-clicking a tab or pressing Ctrl+F1 (Cmd+F1 on macOS); I kept those because you only asked to remove the button.

The ribbon tests pass, including a new check that the spinner is flush with the bar's right edge. The full suite has the same 5 failures as last time, from the code-to-spec, spec-reading and answer-selection tests; none of them touch the ribbon.

- **Spinner:** it's in the ribbon's right container, which only appears while something is running. When the ribbon is collapsed, it sits after the row of commands. The list of running work still opens beneath it and is kept inside the window. I haven't looked at it in the running app.
- **Left side:** it now holds just the project indicator, and the tabs start straight after it.
- The code changes are in `src/ribbon/mod.rs`, with matching test updates in `src/main_window.rs`.

**The spec now disagrees with the code.** `spec/ui/components/ribbon/index.pi` still puts the spinner in the left container, says the right container holds nothing, and describes the chevron button. I left the spec alone as instructed, so it needs a Spec pass (for example, Send to Spec on this task) to match.
